values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The line is the former U-T Offshore System, bought from Enbridge by Delfin's parent company to bring onshore gas to the Delfin floating LNG export project, according to an Argus Media report from November 2015.

verifications.note: Argus Media, Nov 2015: Delfin's parent bought the abandoned 42-inch, 30-mile U-T Offshore System from Enbridge to access onshore gas for Delfin LNG.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already says yes and Delfin FLNG Terminal. An Argus Media report from November 2015 confirms the tie, so the ref is added with the same values.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: Enbridge and Texas LNG agreed in January 2022 to expand Valley Crossing to deliver 720 million cubic feet per day to Texas LNG, with a 10-mile lateral to the terminal, according to Oil & Gas Journal.

verifications.note: OGJ 2022: Valley Crossing expansion to deliver 720 MMcf/d to Texas LNG for at least 20 years; 10-mile lateral built to extend the pipeline to Texas LNG.

records.researcher_notes: The 10-mile lateral matches this row's length. An earlier 2020 deal with Annova LNG for a nine-mile lateral on the same pipeline was not used, since Annova is a different project.

values.AssociatedLNGTerminal: West Delta LNG Deepwater Port Terminal
values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The Federal Register notice of the 2019 license application says gas would reach the West Delta LNG export platform through a 30-inch subsea pipeline from the Venice pretreatment plant.

verifications.note: Federal Register notice Sept 2019: liquefaction-ready gas supplied by Venice Pretreatment Plant and a proposed 30-inch subsea pipeline terminating at the gas arrival platform.

records.researcher_notes: The sheet already says yes and the terminal name. The notice describes the 30-inch subsea feed line without using this row's name, so the tier is medium. The terminal license application was later ended by the Maritime Administration.

records.pipeline_name: Western Energy Storage and Transportation Header Project

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: A 2018 Oil & Gas Journal report on the project's open season says the line could serve West Coast LNG exports, including through Energia Costa Azul in Baja California, Mexico.

verifications.note: OGJ 2018 open season report: possible markets include West Coast LNG exports, including via Energia Costa Azul near Ensenada, Mexico.

records.researcher_notes: LNG exports are one of several markets named for this project, and Costa Azul is named only as a possible route. No terminal is written because the source does not tie the line to one terminal. The project was cancelled.
